newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants rules on gene-maize labelling.
newsitem.headline: France wants rules on gene-maize labelling.

text.p: France said on Monday that it will approve the sale and production of gene-modified maize only when labelling rules are in place.
"(Farm minister) Philippe Vasseur stresses that he will not authorise the release (of gene-maize) as long as the labelling issue has not been settled," the farm ministry said in a statement.

On March 18 the European Commission approved the sale of genetically altered maize in the EU but the approval was accompanied of a Commission undertaking to revise laws to allow for the labelling of gene-modified species.
Existing EU rules do not allow obligatory labelling to show that a product is genetically-modified.
The ministry said France will ask the Commission to speed up plans to adapt EU rules in order to provide better consumer information.
But if it takes too long to change EU rules, France will take measures at national level "to ensure (consumer) information and transparency," the statement said.
The measures will be decided in close association with representatives from the agro-food and animal feed industries and with consummer organisations, it said.
The statement also specified that French farmers will be allowed to grow gene-modified maize only after the ministry clears the release of gene-modified maize on the French market.
This could be a rather lengthy process as gene-modified specifies must be listed in the official register of species and plants grown in France, ministry sources said.
This will allow producers to choose between using regular or genetically-modified seeds.
European consummers and environment groups have opposed the release of gene-altered maize in the EU, arguing there may be possible environmental effects.
